title: Tanzanian Coconut Chutney
community: Zanzibar and the Swahili coast — the coastal condiment
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Chatni ya Nazi — fresh grated coconut blended with green chilli, coriander, garlic, and lemon into a fragrant, cooling condiment. The coastal Tanzanian condiment that accompanies biriani, pilau, and grilled fish — the cooling counterpoint to spiced food.
longDesc: Coconut chutney is the cooling coastal condiment — where pili pili brings heat, chatni ya Nazi brings cooling freshness. Made from fresh grated coconut, it is one of the great accompaniments of the Tanzanian coast.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh grated coconut (or desiccated, rehydrated)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until you reach a coarse, slightly chunky paste.
Add water a little at a time to reach the right consistency.
Taste and adjust lemon, sugar, and salt.
chefTips: Fresh coconut makes a far superior chutney — use it if available.
A slightly coarse texture is more authentic.
The sugar balances the chilli — do not omit.
cookingScience: Fresh coconut contains lauric acid (a medium-chain fatty acid) which acts as a mild natural preservative — allowing the chutney to last 2—3 days in the refrigerator.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh Zanzibar coconut — locally grown with zero food miles.
culturalNote: Chatni ya Nazi is the Zanzibar table's cooling balance — the condiment that makes the heavily spiced biriani and pilau approachable for all heat levels.
